content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], thank you for sharing your project details. I am using a [product_name] controller [article_no] and have a Visual Basic program that identifies the controller’s inputs and outputs via ethernet. I’ve also tried using a third-party Android app to access the device by its IP, but this causes my Visual Basic application to fail—possibly due to an IP conflict? I ran your code in VB and encountered the same issue. Could you please offer some advice?

Hello [user_name], When you attempt to connect both [product_name] development software and the Visual Basic application to a single device, a port conflict will occur since both applications use port 10001 for communication. Regards,

Hello [user_name], I’ve added some pictures and screenshots of the Visual Basic application. The VB program accurately reads the status of the [product_name] controller [article_no]. The issue arises when trying to access the same device from a website or Android phone using its IP—the Visual Basic app then stops working. I am hoping to resolve this for a small project. I appreciate any suggestions that could help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users connecting to a [product_name] controller with both a Visual Basic application and a third-party Android app encounter network port conflicts, resulting in the Visual Basic app failing. The problem is due to both programs trying to use the same network port (10001) to communicate with the device at the same time, highlighting limitations in simultaneous multi-platform access to the controller.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to be able to monitor and control the [product_name] controller from multiple applications, such as Visual Basic and Android apps, concurrently without experiencing connection or port conflicts.
pain_keywords: cannot access PLC from multiple devices
